subject: AWS Marketplace: activation CTA and trial length guidance
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-06T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace listing: activation CTA & trial duration

Alex —

Thanks for the walkthrough today. A couple of items we need to lock down before we hand the listing to procurement:

- Trial length: can Redwood support a 30-day free trial on the AWS listing, or are we constrained to 14 days because of the SKU entitlements? ACME prefers 30 to align with customer trials.
- CTA language: we currently default to "Start free trial" on our site, but marketplace rules suggested we might need "Request free trial" or "Contact seller" for Private Offers. Which CTA maps best to a self-serve activation?
- Any billing footnotes we should include (metering, post-trial conversion)? Procurement will push back if this isn't explicit.

I've attached a short walkthrough of the ACME desired flow (acme-walkthrough.pdf). Can you confirm recommended copy blocks and whether we should change our landing CTA?

Appreciate it —
Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Partnerships, ACME AI

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeai.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-06T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing: activation CTA & trial duration

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary and the walkthrough PDF. High level answers up front: yes, we can support a 30-day trial on the AWS listing, but the CTA and entitlements depend on whether you want a public SaaS listing (self-serve) or a Private Offer (gated). Quick bullets: 

- Public listing (self-serve): "Start free trial" is fine and maps to a direct activation flow. We can wire a PAYG SKU or a 30-day trial SKU.
- Private Offer: marketplace UX typically surfaces "Request trial" or "Contact seller" because procurement signs a PO; activation is handled via Private Offer entitlements and manual provisioning.
- Billing footnotes: we recommend calling out trial auto-conversion (on/off), what metrics are metered (tokens/min or monthly MAU), and refund/rollback policy. Short example footnote included below.

I'll loop Kim and Marissa to propose two hero CTA variants and the precise footnote language we should show beneath pricing. Marissa — can you draft the hero copy variants that match a 30-day self-serve trial and a gated Private Offer flow? Kim — can you confirm SKU and entitlement names so we don't create ambiguous SKUs in the catalog?

Proposed short billing footnote (draft):
"Trial duration: 30 days. After trial, customers are billed at the selected PAYG tier. Usage is metered per 1k tokens; no automatic refunds for overages. Private offers require procurement approval and may include different trial terms."

Looping you back shortly with file attachments.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-06T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Marketplace listing: activation CTA & trial duration — copy + SKU ask

Kim / Marissa —

Forwarding Jordan's note. Key asks:
1) Two hero CTA + subtitle variants we can present to ACME: one optimized for public self-serve 30-day activation; one for Private Offer (contact/request). Keep copy tight for the marketplace hero area (headline + 1-line subhead + CTA).
2) Confirm SKU names and an entitlement plan: we should propose a trial SKU (TRIAL-30) and a PAYG SKU (PAYG-1k). If Private Offer is chosen, procurement will need a SKU mapping doc for their PO.
3) Short pricing footnote (one line) and a longer 1-paragraph explanation for the detail modal.

Attachments I added to the draft: hero_variants_v3.docx and sku-mapping-proposal.xlsx. Use the shared HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-98765) as the single source of truth for copy approvals.

Marissa: can you prioritize the hero variants? Two options by 11:30am PT would be ideal so I can sync back to Jordan before lunch.

Thanks —
Alex

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeai.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-06T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing: activation CTA & trial duration

Jordan —

Quick update and concrete options (see attached hero_variants_v3.docx for exact text snippets):

Option A — Public, self-serve (recommended if you want immediate activation):
Headline: "Start building with Redwood Inference on AWS Marketplace"
Subhead: "Free 30-day trial with PAYG billing after — metered per 1k tokens"
CTA: "Start free trial"
Footnote (one-liner): "30-day free trial; usage billed per 1k tokens after trial."
SKU mapping: TRIAL-30 -> PAYG-1k (see sku-mapping-proposal.xlsx).

Option B — Private Offer (recommended for enterprise procurement workflows):
Headline: "Request a trial via Private Offer"
Subhead: "Procurement-managed trial and unique pricing for enterprise terms"
CTA: "Request trial"
Footnote (one-liner): "Private Offer trials are provisioned after procurement approval; contact sales for details."

Notes on implementation:
- If ACME wants the 30-day self-serve trial, we can create the TRIAL-30 SKU and configure auto-conversion settings in the marketplace catalog. Auto-conversion is optional; if you prefer an opt-in conversion we can disable auto-billing and notify customers before charge.
- For private offers we will supply ACME with the SKU mapping and a short procurement checklist for their PO team.

Next steps: if you confirm which option you prefer I will: (1) update the marketplace hero copy and CTA; (2) send the SKU mapping and procurement checklist; (3) request a marketplace review date.

Which path would ACME prefer?

Best —
Alex Martinez
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: hero_variants_v3.docx (hero copy options), sku-mapping-proposal.xlsx (SKU mapping and entitlements)
